crossrefs.text: A voice says, “Cry out!” And I asked, “What should I cry out?” “All flesh is like grass, and all its glory like the flowers of the field.
The grass withers and the flowers fall, but the word of our God stands forever.”
For we were born yesterday and know nothing; our days on earth are but a shadow.
For, “All flesh is like grass, and all its glory like the flowers of the field; the grass withers and the flowers fall,
As for man, his days are like grass— he blooms like a flower of the field;
when the wind passes over, it vanishes, and its place remembers it no more.
For we are foreigners and strangers in Your presence, as were all our forefathers. Our days on earth are like a shadow, without hope.
You do not even know what will happen tomorrow! What is your life? You are a mist that appears for a little while and then vanishes.
In the days to come, Jacob will take root. Israel will bud and blossom and fill the whole world with fruit.
Then a shoot will spring up from the stump of Jesse, and a Branch from his roots will bear fruit.
When a man dies, will he live again? All the days of my hard service I will wait, until my renewal comes.

And you, O king, saw a watcher, a holy one, coming down from heaven and saying: ‘Cut down the tree and destroy it, but leave the stump with its roots in the ground, with a band of iron and bronze around it, in the tender grass of the field. Let him be drenched with the dew of heaven, and graze with the beasts of the field till seven times pass him by.’

You will be driven away from mankind, and your dwelling will be with the beasts of the field. You will feed on grass like an ox and be drenched with the dew of heaven, and seven times shall pass you by, until you acknowledge that the Most High rules over the kingdom of mankind and gives it to whom He wishes.
He tears me down on every side until I am gone; He uproots my hope like a tree.
before I go—never to return— to a land of darkness and gloom,
to a land of utter darkness, of deep shadow and disorder, where even the light is like darkness.”
Listen, I tell you a mystery: We will not all sleep, but we will all be changed—
in an instant, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, the dead will be raised imperishable, and we will be changed.
“Have I not stored up these things, sealed up within My vaults?
that You should seek my iniquity and search out my sin—
“Is not man consigned to labor on earth? Are not his days like those of a hired hand?
Why would any of you consider it incredible that God raises the dead?
Does it please You to oppress me, to reject the work of Your hands and favor the schemes of the wicked?
Though He slay me, I will hope in Him. I will still defend my ways to His face.
The sky receded like a scroll being rolled up, and every mountain and island was moved from its place.
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
And behold, I will bring floodwaters upon the earth to destroy every creature under the heavens that has the breath of life. Everything on the earth will perish.

And every living thing that moved upon the earth perished—birds, livestock, animals, every creature that swarms upon the earth, and all mankind. Of all that was on dry land, everything that had the breath of life in its nostrils died. And every living thing on the face of the earth was destroyed—man and livestock, crawling creatures and birds of the air; they were blotted out from the earth, and only Noah and those with him in the ark remained.
As she was dying, the women attending to her said, “Do not be afraid, for you have given birth to a son!” But she did not respond or pay any heed.
When they lifted up their eyes from afar, they could barely recognize Job. They began to weep aloud, and each man tore his robe and threw dust in the air over his head.
When a man dies, will he live again? All the days of my hard service I will wait, until my renewal comes.
You who tear yourself in anger— should the earth be forsaken on your account, or the rocks be moved from their place?
